records.title: The Tower is the loom of the Three Fates, the great frame on which the world was strung.
records.body: The Hearth folk hold that the Three Fates wove the world on the Tower. To them the Tower simply is, as a mountain is.

records.title: The Spinner, the Measurer and the Cutter wove the world.
records.body: The pantheon of the lower floors: the Three Fates.

records.title: Magic is the Fates' gift, lent to those who learn the proper rites.
records.body: Casting is ritual in the Hearth, and nobody there has ever doubted where it comes from.

records.title: The dead are in the Tower's walls.
records.body: A persistent folk belief, held everywhere. Hauntings cluster near the old ruins.

records.title: The spirits are ancestors, demons or elementals.
records.body: What the spirits that binders treat with are widely thought to be. The Hearth folk pray to them as ancestors.

records.title: The humming chamber beneath the shrine is holy ground, and no priest can say why.
records.body: A Fates' shrine in the lower Hearth is built, as many are, on a far older chamber that still faintly hums. The priests call it holy ground and cannot explain it.

records.title: The marks on the old plates are holy script.
records.body: How the inscribed plates in the old chambers are read by those who cannot read them.

records.title: What the Tower is stands written on the old plates, for those who collect the inscriptions and reconcile them.
records.body: The Concordance collects ruin-inscriptions and tries to reconcile them.

records.title: The Tower is a machine, and magic is its by-product.
records.body: The claim of a heretical minority. The orthodox of the Concordance find it blasphemous or simply absurd.

records.title: We use half.
records.body: A phrase the Concordance only whispers.
voice: — whispered among those who read the old plates

records.title: The seven points of the body have names on the old plates: Lumbar Anchor, Sacral Spool, Plexal Bellows, Sub-Clavicular Nodes, Glottal Reed, Pineal Resonator, Coronal Aperture.
records.body: The scholarly names of the seven chakras belong to the Concordance and the old plates. Sects and common folk name the points by location only.

records.title: The song is not only power but a lock, and to silence it is to open a door onto whatever the Tower was built over.
records.body: A rumour of the highest ruins, kept in Concordance marginalia. Nobody has proof either way. A speaker may fear it or doubt it, and may never settle it.

records.title: A rune is a sentence in the First Script, the language older than speech that holds the world together.
records.body: A carved glyph is one true sentence, set into stone or steel or skin so that it holds its breath until struck. The carving is done in calm; the word is woken later, with a strike to its heart.

records.title: A glyph must be given room to breathe, or its voice arrives crowded.
records.body: What every apprentice learns first. Marks set too close trip over one another; marks given their proper spacing speak in turn. To the Scribes it is manners: a word said too fast is a word said wrong.

records.title: Tight, sharp strokes carry heat and lightning; long, soft strokes carry weight and patience.
records.body: The hand chooses the rune's temper by how sharply it turns.

records.title: The quiet death: a word that argues with itself goes cold, and the Scribe feels the sting of it in the hand.
records.body: One of the two ruins of a clumsy rune. The strokes deaden one another and the glyph fizzles.

records.title: The loud death: a sentence bent back into its own mouth feeds on itself until it bursts.
records.body: The second ruin, and far the worse. Every apprentice is shown the scorch-marks on old workshop floors on their first day.
voice: Never close a word upon itself in anger.

records.title: A rune that bursts and kills its maker was carved in anger: a word written with a hot heart turns on its writer.
records.body: What the guilds say when a great rune bursts. So apprentices are made to carve only when calm, to breathe slow, and never to cut a line while wroth.

records.title: Trace the glyph once in the air and count a slow breath along each line: if the breath comes ragged or runs out, the word will arrive crowded.
records.body: The Breath-Test, done before a glyph is woken. Hedge-Scribes swear by it.

records.title: Spacing is checked with a measuring-cord; the Breath-Test is superstition.
records.body: Academy-Scribes use the cord instead, and arrive at the same answer.

records.title: Honest stone speaks truer than cut stone.
records.body: A glyph carved by a steady living hand into rough, natural stone holds its temper far better than one machined into smooth synthetic slate, which cracks at the smallest wrong note. Glyphs etched by mold are mistrusted; their work is said to be tuneless.

records.title: A master's true glyph is taught to no one and copied to no one.
records.body: Master Scribes hoard a small number of perfected sentences, pressed whole into a work like a single stamped seal. To own a master's true glyph is to own a fortune.

records.title: The old master-glyphs are perfect: the ancients said the last word.
records.body: The Scribes hold the craft complete, handed down from an age wiser than this one.
voice: No hand will better the Ninefold Seal.

records.title: The body is a river of Chi that runs in meridians and gathers at the seven Chakras; the points along the meridians are gates.
records.body: What any sect elder will say has been known for a thousand years.

records.title: The three great Chakras are the Pineal at the brow, the Sub-Clavicular at the heart's gate and the Lumbar at the root of the spine; the lesser four sit at the crown, the throat, the navel and the seat.
records.body: Each of the lesser four has its office: the crown drinks the world's weather, the throat gives the river voice, the navel drives the bellows of a blow, and the seat draws the thread up from the deep well.

records.title: In Mountain Stance the warrior widens and sinks until the mountain lends its weight.
records.body: A stance is how a fighter borrows from the world. Willow Stance keeps the channels loose and quick, bending so the strike snaps back like a branch released. Drawn-Bow Stance coils the body's river backward so it can be loosed all at once.

records.title: To seal a gate is to close a door so the river finds another path.
records.body: Sealing redirects the current down a quieter meridian when the main road is shut.

records.title: A Chakra may be steeped in one of the five elements, wood, fire, earth, metal or water, the way a blade is tempered.
records.body: Years of one discipline soak a gate in its element. A gate steeped in fire will not take water until the fire has wholly cooled from it, a fading the masters say takes as long as the setting did. An elder's gates are read like the rings of a tree.

records.title: Within every gate the breath turns between yin and yang: strike from yang, recover in yin, and never loose a great blow from a gate at full ebb.
records.body: The balance is never still; it tilts with exertion and stillness, anger and calm. Students learn to read their own tilt the way a sailor reads weather.

records.title: A strike must be given, not forced: the hand should arrive at the moment the breath crests, as the wave meets the shore.
records.body: The teaching of the Quiet-River Sect.

records.title: A blow that dies in the hand was struck from an unclean gate, or anger was let into the Flow.
records.body: A student who strikes too soon or too late is told the Flow was impure; the backlash leaves him winded and aching. Harm, to the masters, is always a failure of spirit.

records.title: Master Vale of the Coiling Path turned his river inward with a devouring form, and it swallowed him whole.
records.body: The cautionary tale every novice learns. Vale, the most gifted fighter of his generation, sought a way to make the river feed upon itself so that each strike fed the next without end. For a season he was unstoppable; then his own power doubled upon itself until it burst the gates from within. The sects forbid the devouring forms as wisdom, not cowardice: the river turned back on itself does not stop.

records.title: The ancestral forms are finished: a thousand generations of masters have carried human potential to its summit.
records.body: What remains for the student is only to attain the forms, never to surpass them. To suggest that a stance might be made twice as powerful would be heard as arrogance, even heresy.

records.title: Everything in the world has a true name, and to sing that name in its proper measure is to make the world remember what it is.
records.body: Reality, the Cantors teach, is not commanded but agreed with. You do not force the stone; you sing the stone's true song until the world agrees, and it is so.

records.title: A chant is not only its notes but its measure: the rests are counted as carefully as the tones.
records.body: It is the spacing between syllables that lets the song hold its shape. A novice spends years learning to breathe the rests correctly before ever being trusted with a true name.

records.title: The Ground-Ohm, the Mendicant's Rest, is sung first in nearly every working.
records.body: A low sustained drone that lays a steady foundation, the bed on which all else is built. Healers open with it; without a true Ohm, nothing after it will hold.

records.title: Kharrian's Stride carries a working's power outward and makes a road for it across distance.
records.body: A percussive marching chant of clipped mid syllables: Khar, Khar. Wardens sing it to send their songs along walls and rivers.

records.title: The Severing Sa releases a working all at once, and it is sung last.
records.body: A hissing chant of sharp high cries: a healer's closing breath, a striker's loosed arrow. It is the chant that acts.

records.title: To sing a word the world refuses strikes the singer dumb.
records.body: The dread of the false name. The dissonant word shatters the steady drone beneath it and steals the voice for hours, sometimes days. Cantors will not speak certain near-true names aloud.
voice: Better to hum than to misname.

records.title: The Unending Note fed upon itself and swallowed the choir that sang it.
records.body: The warning-legend every Cantor knows. The chant grew louder with every breath and left an empty abbey still faintly ringing. It is why no song is sung in a closed loop, and why the songbooks forbid any chant that answers its own echo.

records.title: The songbooks are complete: the old masters sang reality to its very limit.
records.body: The Order holds that no voice could ever draw more from the world than the liturgy already does. To sing a chant exactly as written is to sing it as fully as it can be sung.

records.title: The world is thick with Listeners, and each one carries a single eternal note it has sung since before the first hearth.
records.body: Listeners are spirits, ancestors, hungry elementals and the half-named dead. To work the great magics you go out, find a Listener and talk it into lending you its voice.
voice: A binder casts nothing. A binder only sings until something stronger says yes.

records.title: A binder's first lesson is the ear, to hear the Listener's note under the world's noise; the second is the throat, to sing it back so truly that the spirit believes it has found kin.
records.body: The Throat-Kin learn, above all, to listen and answer.

records.title: When the note is wrong the air shivers, and that is the Quarrel; silence is the lock.
records.body: A wobble, a throb in the teeth, which the old women call the Quarrel. As the binder bends her voice toward the spirit's true note the Quarrel slows, softens and at last falls silent. A silent air means the spirit has agreed.
voice: Sing until the air stops arguing.

records.title: The greater the god, the truer the note it demands.
records.body: Everyone knows a small spirit forgives a clumsy song, but a great or proud Listener will not. Sing even slightly false to a proud one and the Quarrel never stills; it only grows teeth.

records.title: Vareth the Long Cold is a frost-elemental of the high passes: her note is low and slow, her power vast and her pride immense.
records.body: One of the Three Named Listeners told to every apprentice. Bind her and you may raise rivers of ice and bridges from nothing. She suffers no false singer, and the passes are full of binders frozen mid-song.

records.title: Old Grandfather Ember is an ancestor-spirit of the forge-clans, warm and forgiving.
records.body: One of the Three Named Listeners. His note is easy to find and he lends gladly, but he lends little. Apprentices learn on him because his Quarrel is gentle and he rarely turns.

records.title: The Gull-Throat, Skerrin, is a fickle wind-spirit of the coast whose note will not hold still.
records.body: One of the Three Named Listeners, neither great nor small but restless. Even a locked pact with Skerrin must be re-sung constantly, for he loves to slip the leash and laugh.

records.title: A pact is never taken; it is kept.
records.body: You must hold the song the whole while the spirit serves you; let your breath wander and the bargain frays. So the Throat-Kin offer the proper things, true names spoken aloud, an oath repeated, salt or blood or a remembered song, because the offering keeps the singer's mind on the note.

records.title: Honor its name, or it turns on you.
records.body: The first taboo of all. When a binder's song fails a spirit she has called, the Quarrel comes roaring back and the lent power turns and pours back down the song into the singer. The Turning is always blamed on disrespect: a name said wrong, an oath half-meant, pride that reached past the singer's throat.

records.title: Halvarr the Bold sang to the Long Cold with a note that was almost true, and she turned on him.
records.body: The cautionary tale told to every apprentice. Halvarr would not learn on Grandfather Ember like the others. He found Vareth's note, almost; the Quarrel never fully stilled, but he reached for her strength. For one breath he raised a tower of ice that dwarfed anything a mortal could shape; then her cold came back down his own song. They found him in the spring, a man of blue glass, mouth still open on a note he never quite found.

records.title: To bind the greatest spirit is to hold the very ceiling of power.
records.body: The proud thing all the Throat-Kin believe.

records.title: Even the one who sings perfectly holds but half of what the spirit keeps, and no living mouth has ever learned the rest.
records.body: The elders who watched Halvarr swore that even his tower of ice was but a sliver of what Vareth withheld.

records.title: An operator-plate under a Fates' shrine, in a script no Fate ever spoke
records.body: First contact with the mystery. Nothing is explained, but the certainty cracks.

records.title: A spirit under the shrine murmurs a fragment of a dead tongue
records.body: Found on the same errand as the operator-plate.

records.title: An echo-vault shows ghost-figures weaving: the builders were people
records.body: They are not gods or giants.

records.title: The first recovered fragment of lost method, and the phrase 'we use half'
records.body: From here the ceiling is a known absence.

records.title: The spirits clearly answer to song
records.body: The heretic theory of the Concordance stops sounding absurd.

records.title: Echo-vaults replay the unweaving itself
records.body: Here the player learns what happened.

records.title: Half-readable operator-plates spell out the builders' purpose: to make the great song eternal
records.body: To stop having to hold the world up by hand; to become gods.

records.title: The revelation that the spirits are the builders
records.body: Every pact the player has made was a conversation with the dead who made all this.

records.title: The apex gods resolve into prior Conductors
records.body: Stranger and sadder than worship made them.

records.title: The eternal cycle is the Discord
records.body: The catastrophe is not a risk of finishing Theos but the definition of it.

records.title: The Tower is a machine: a hundred-register resonator raised over a puncture into the Chaos Matrix.
records.body: Each of its hundred floors is a tuned register of the instrument. Its function was to make reality editable.

records.title: The Weave is an artifact of the Tower: magic can be worked because the Tower exists.
records.body: Outside the Tower's influence the world is hard and fixed. Within its field the boundary to the Chaos Matrix is thin, and Prime Mana can be drawn and instructed.

records.title: The Tower was built by a precursor civilization, the Tuners, who held the complete mathematics of the Weave.
records.body: They ran it near 100% of Capacity (E8). They did not carve runes or chant like their inheritors; they knew the true shape of every string.

records.title: Theos is the master resonance the Tower sustained: a song, not a god.
records.body: The Tuners named the great stabilising chord Theos, the song that holds the world. The Tower is named for the song. That a later age mistook the song for a deity is the central irony of the setting.

records.title: The Great Discord: the Tuners tried to make Theos self-sustaining, the cycle ran away and they were unwoven.
records.body: The cycle's loop gain slipped the stability threshold; this is the civilization-scale instance of the runaway failure mode (E6/E7). The Tuners were not killed so much as unwoven into drifting strings and fragments.

records.title: The spirits and the discordant masses are the unwoven Tuners: the dead builders.
records.body: The drifting remnants are the spirits or Listeners that Spirit Magic binds; the corrupted fragments are the discordant masses that haunt the Tower.

records.title: The ~50% ceiling is lost know-how, not physics: every rune, form, chant and pact realises about half of what its structure could bear.
records.body: After the fall the craft was rebuilt from ruins and superstition, and only about half of what the Tuners knew was recovered. Capacity (E8) is not capped. Recovering the other half is the Understanding progression.

records.title: The Three Fates are a folk memory of the Tuners' operating triad: spool, measure and route, cut.
records.body: The Spinner, the Measurer and the Cutter are the three stages of weaving: spool Prime Mana from the Matrix, measure and route it into a tensioned graph, cut it to release the effect.

records.title: The ruins are the working parts of the dead machine, and the operator-plates carry the Tuners' notation, which is the real mathematics.
records.body: Tuning galleries and choir-halls are resonating chambers; echo-vaults replay fragments of the builders at work; the conductor's relics lie near the summit. Reading them is how the lost half is recovered.

records.title: The Tower survived half-detuned; its broken song is why reality near it is soft and why volatility rises with height.
records.body: The upper floors sit closest to the conductor's gallery and the widest part of the puncture. The residual detuning is the environment variable the engine models.

records.title: The apex gods are prior Conductors: climbers who took the seat and never left.
records.body: Every climber who chose to sustain Theos by hand became the god that later climbers find and mythologise.

records.title: The dream is the disaster: a self-sustaining Theos is the runaway condition itself.
records.body: A cycle whose gain never decays is the runaway condition (E6/E7). The Tuners did not fail by accident; what they wanted is, mathematically, the catastrophe.

records.title: The Seal is false: nothing waits behind the silence, and the song can be ended safely.
records.body: The dread that Theos is a lock is in-world myth only. Directive for writers and designers: hint it, let characters fear it, never script a payoff that proves or disproves it.

records.title: Understanding can release the unwoven: in the Mending and the Silence the builders finish their unraveling and rest.
records.body: The Tower's haunting ends not by exorcism but by someone finally understanding what was done. In the Repetition the player simply joins them.

records.title: Deadening: opposed contributions cancel and the working goes silent; at root it is a mismatch of length or timing (E4).
records.body: One of the two failure modes of every interface, stated on the Runes, Chanting and Martial Arts explaining pages. The caster takes mild feedback harm.

records.title: Runaway: a working that feeds itself builds loop gain past the stability threshold and detonates as backlash (E6/E7).
records.body: The second failure mode of every interface, stated on the Runes, Chanting, Martial Arts and Spirit Magic explaining pages.

records.title: A spirit is an external anchor with a fixed frequency; matching its song is the coherence lock, and the shiver is the mismatch beating toward zero (E5).
records.body: The bargain with an external being justifies the external authoring axis: the graph is sourced from another entity's anchor, not from the caster's body.

records.title: A proud spirit has high dominance, which narrows the tolerance of the lock: a truer match is required (E5).
records.body: Dominance is an interface-side reparameterisation of the tolerance window. No Core change, no new token.

records.title: A pact needs upkeep: the tone must be sustained at a continuous cost, and efficiency drops as it drifts (E9, E10).
records.body: The engine side of what the binders call keeping the bargain.

records.title: A chant is a sequence of timed tones: pitch selects the element, and the spaces between syllables set the lengths from which phase is derived (E1, E2).
records.body: The voice is a token source; the world is the solver. Because a sung voice is analog, chanting forgives small errors and drifts more than a quantised interface.

records.title: A rune is a hand-drawn specification of an oscillator graph: curvature is frequency, carving pressure is amplitude, and spacing becomes phase through propagation delay (E1, E2).
records.body: Nothing magical happens in the rune itself; the substrate holds the graph still until discharge. There are no fixed elements, only a smooth function of tightness.

records.title: A rune fails by its geometry alone; the carver's mood plays no part.
records.body: The guild lesson about anger keeps young hands steady, but the reason it gives is wrong.

records.title: Hand-carved, analog work tolerates wider mismatch than synthetic work (E5).
records.body: Sloppy precision is punished, but organic imprecision is forgiven by design.

records.title: The body's meridian web is a graph that already exists, organised around seven chakra points; Chi is its oscillation, and a stance changes path lengths and so phase (E1, E2).
records.body: Every caster has the seven points; Martial Arts leans on them hardest. A wide stance lengthens the path so that amplitude builds before it reaches the effector. Sealing a gate deactivates a point and forces a reroute.

records.title: Each chakra point holds at most one elemental attunement, which deepens slowly and can be retrained only once it has fully faded, and a Yin-Yang polarity that is a dynamic balance.
records.body: Both mechanics are planned for a later milestone; the data shapes are fixed now.

layers.title: An academy-Scribe
layers.body: Synthetic speaker for the PoC scenarios, not a character of the game. Checks spacing with a measuring-cord.

layers.title: Academy-Scribes
layers.body: Scribes of the academies. They check spacing with a measuring-cord and call the Breath-Test superstition.

layers.title: Scribes of the Rune-houses
layers.body: Those who can write the First Script. They carve glyphs into stone, steel or skin and wake them later with a strike to the heart.

lens.thinks_from: The world is held together by the First Script, a language older than speech
lens.stance: the craft is complete; a student's task is to copy the old sentences ever more faithfully
lens.speaks_to: apprentices, in workshop rules and grave warnings

layers.title: A Throat-Kin binder
layers.body: Synthetic speaker for the PoC scenarios, not a character of the game. Teaches the ear first and the throat second.

layers.title: Throat-Kin
layers.body: Pact-witches and spirit-speakers, also called binders. They do not spin power from their own breath: they find a Listener and talk it into lending its voice.

lens.thinks_from: The world is thick with Listeners, each carrying one eternal note
lens.stance: listen and answer; a binder casts nothing
lens.speaks_to: apprentices, in sayings and cautionary tales

layers.title: A Cantor of the Measured Voice
layers.role: singer of the Order who keeps a songbook
layers.body: Synthetic speaker for the PoC scenarios, not a character of the game. Sings the chants exactly as the songbook records them.

layers.title: The Order of the Measured Voice
layers.body: The great tradition of the Cantors: a monastic line of singers who keep the songbooks, in which every proven chant is recorded note for note, silence for silence.

layers.title: Cantors
layers.body: Singers of true names. The old and the proud among them prefer to be called Namers.

lens.thinks_from: Everything has a true name; reality is not commanded but agreed with
lens.stance: serene certainty that the old masters sang reality to its limit
lens.speaks_to: novices, who learn to breathe the rests before they are trusted with a true name

layers.title: A hedge-Scribe
layers.body: Synthetic speaker for the PoC scenarios, not a character of the game. Carves and wakes glyphs, and tests every one by breath before waking it.

layers.title: Hedge-Scribes
layers.body: Scribes outside the academies. They swear by the Breath-Test.

layers.title: Scribes of the Rune-houses
layers.body: Those who can write the First Script. They carve glyphs into stone, steel or skin and wake them later with a strike to the heart.

layers.title: A heretic of the Concordance
layers.body: Synthetic speaker for the PoC scenarios, not a character of the game. Holds the minority's claim about the Tower.

layers.title: The heretical minority of the Concordance
layers.body: A minority within the Concordance whose claim about the Tower the orthodox find blasphemous or simply absurd.

layers.title: The Concordance
layers.body: Scholars known in the world as those who read the old plates. They are the force that pulls belief toward the truth, though they know less than they think.

lens.thinks_from: The old plates and ruin-inscriptions can be collected and reconciled

layers.title: A reader of the old plates

layers.title: An elder of the Quiet-River Sect
layers.role: sect elder who teaches novices the ancestral forms
layers.body: Synthetic speaker for the PoC scenarios, not a character of the game. Teaches the forms and tells the tale of Master Vale.

layers.title: The Quiet-River Sect
layers.body: The oldest of the orthodox sects. It teaches that a strike must be given, not forced.

layers.title: Martial sects
layers.body: The sects of the martial tradition. Their masters have no use for numbers: mastery is the long moral and physical labor of making breath, intent and movement one unbroken thing, which they name Flow.

lens.thinks_from: The body is a river of Chi; mastery is discipline, not calculation
lens.stance: the ancestral forms are finished; to surpass them is arrogance, even heresy
lens.speaks_to: novices, through the forms and through cautionary tales

layers.title: A keeper of a Fates' shrine
layers.role: keeper of a Fates' shrine in the lower Hearth
layers.body: Synthetic speaker for the PoC scenarios, not a character of the game. Keeps a shrine that stands on an older chamber which still faintly hums.

layers.title: Fates-cult
layers.body: Priests and keepers of the Fates' shrines. Many shrines are built on far older chambers that the priests call holy ground and cannot explain.

layers.title: Hearth folk
layers.body: The people of the lower floors. They hold magic to be the Three Fates' gift and have never doubted it.

lens.thinks_from: The Three Fates wove the world, and the Tower is their loom
lens.stance: certain; the Tower simply is, as a mountain is
